events.title: Q1 2024 Futu Holdings Ltd Earnings Call

content.text:
Operator
Hello, ladies and gentlemen. Welcome to Futu Holdings Q4 and full year 2023 earnings conference call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After management's prepared remarks, there will be a Q&A session. Today's conference call is being recorded. If you have any objections, you may disconnect at this time. I would now like to turn the conference over to your host for today's conference call, Daniel Yuan, Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR at Futu. Please go ahead, sir.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Thanks, operator, and thank you all for joining us today to discuss our Q4 and full year 2023 earnings results. Joining me on the call today are Mr. Leaf Li, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Arthur Chen, Chief Financial Officer, and Robin Xu, Senior Vice President. As a reminder, today's call may include forward-looking statements, which represent the company's belief regarding future events, which, by their nature, are not certain and are outside of the company's control. Forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties. We caution you that a number of important factors could cause actual results to differ materially from those contained in any forward-looking statements. For more information about the potential risks and uncertainties, please refer to the company's filings with the SEC, including its annual report. With that, I will now turn the call over to Leaf.
Leaf will make his comments in Chinese, and I will translate.
[Foreign language]
Thank you all for joining our earnings call today. In Q4, we added over 59,000 paying clients. Our total paying clients as of year-end reached over 1.7 million, representing 15% growth year-over-year and exceeding our guidance.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
第四季度，新加坡的获客继续保持高速增长。在高利率和市场高度波动的背景下，货币基金持续获得客户青睐。十二月，我们与富敦基金管理公司合作，独家分销了一只新元货币基金。这只基金也是新加坡市面上唯一一只专门面向零售投资者的T+0新元货币基金。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Client acquisition in Singapore sustained high growth into Q4. Money market funds continued to garner significant client interest amid high interest rates and market volatility. In December, we became the first and only distributor of Fullerton Fund Management Singapore dollar-denominated money market fund, the only T+0 Singapore dollar money market fund for retail investors in Singapore.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
凭借我们丰富的市场信息、全面的金融数据以及活跃的社区，我们在日本持续占领用户心智。根据data.ai的数据显示，第四季度，moomoo App在日本的日均下载量在所有券商中排名前三，超过了本地老牌券商野村証券和松井証券。随着日経指数录得显著涨幅并不断创下新高，一季度日本的获客数量环比增幅明显。我们持续优化开户流程，减少从用户到有资产客户各个环节中的流失。我们也在持续推进关键产品上线。十二月，我们上线了成长型NISA账户，我们计划在不久之后上线日股交易，也预计会在二季度为香港和新加坡的客户提供日股交易。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
We continue to gain user mindshare in Japan with our rich market information, comprehensive market data, and interactive social community. In Q4, the average daily downloads of moomoo app in Japan ranked top three among all brokers and surpassed those of Nomura and Matsui Securities, according to data.ai. With Nikkei recording remarkable gains and hitting new highs, client acquisition in Japan also showed a notable sequential increase in Q1. We continue to streamline the account opening process to reduce leakage in the conversion funnel and focused on R&D for key investment products. We launched NISA Growth account in December and will soon roll out Japan equities trading. Our clients in Hong Kong and Singapore will also have access to Japan stock trading in Q2.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
第四季度，由于香港市场情绪低迷，本地获客速度放缓。但今年一季度，随着香港股市的复苏有所反弹。在美国，我们继续关注客户质量。新增有资产客户的户均首季度净入金环比增长约30%。在澳大利亚，我们专注于品牌建设以及产品上新，并于四季度上线了现金管理产品。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Client acquisition in Hong Kong slowed down due to sluggish market sentiments, yet rebounded in Q1 along with the recovery of the Hong Kong stock market. In the US, we continue to prioritize client quality over quantity, with the average asset balance of new paying clients in their first quarter of onboarding increasing by over 30% compared to the last quarter. In Australia, we focused on cultivating brand equity and adding new products, including cash management.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
今年的二月二十六日，我们在马来西亚正式上线了证券经纪服务。业务上线以来，获客势头强劲，上线一周内开户客户超过三万人。这是我们所有国际市场中增长最快的。过去三年，我们在新加坡的市占率增长迅猛，品牌影响力辐射范围广，所以我们从上线初期就在马来西亚积累了较高的知
On 26 February 2023, we launched brokerage business in Malaysia and gained significant traction. Over 30,000 clients flocked to our platform within 1 week of the official launch, representing the fastest growth in any of our international markets. We managed to generate high brand awareness in Malaysia from the outset, thanks to our rapid share gain in Singapore over the past 3 years.
今年我们在各个市场都看到了有资产客户强劲的增长势头。今年前两个月的净增有资产客户和净入金规模已经超过去年第四季度。鉴于今年至今为止的强劲势头，我们预计2024年净增35万名有资产客户。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
We observed robust paying client growth across all markets this year. In fact, we attracted more paying clients and net asset inflows in the first two months this year than the entire Q4. Given the strong momentum year to date, we are guiding for 350,000 net new paying clients in 2024.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
客户总资产同比增长16%，环比增长4%，达到4,860亿港元。环比增长主要得益于客户每股资产市值的上涨以及各个市场强劲的净入金。在新加坡，由于各个cohort客户入金都很强劲，客户总资产和平均资产分别环比增长25%和17%，户均资产超过1.7万新元。随着我们的品牌影响力的不断增强，moomoo得到了越来越多高净值人群的青睐。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Total client assets increased by 16% year over year and 4% quarter over quarter to HKD 486 billion. The sequential increase was largely due to robust net asset inflow across all regions, and the market appreciation of our clients' US stock holdings. In Singapore, total client assets and average client assets posted sequential increase of 25% and 17% respectively. Average client assets was over SGD 17,000 due to strong inflows across cohorts. As we continue to build brand equity, moomoo gained traction among high net worth clients in Singapore. As of quarter end, margin financing and securities lending balance increased marginally by 2% quarter over quarter. While we saw an uptick in securities lending balance for US stocks, margin financing balance declined as clients unwound their positions.
Total trading volume was HKD 957 billion, down 12% year-over-year and quarter over quarter. In Q4, Hong Kong and US stock trading volume were down 13% and 12% sequentially. Weak sentiments around Hong Kong equities and lower turnover in US tech stocks dragged total trading volume. Our share gains in the derivatives market in Hong Kong was a bright spot. Hong Kong futures and options trading had 8.5% and 14.7% market share in Q4, respectively. Next, I'd like to invite our CFO, Arthur, to discuss our financial performance.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Leaf and Daniel. Before going through our financial performance, I'd like to give you an update on our latest share repurchase program announced on 11 March 2022. As of 31 December 2023, the expiration day of the program, we had repurchased an aggregate of 11 million ADSs with approximately $365 million total repurchase amount in open market transactions. We have put in place a new share repurchase program which approves and authorizes to repurchase up to $500 million of ADSs before 31 December 2025. Now, please allow me to walk you through our financial performance. All numbers are in HKD unless otherwise noted. Total revenue was HKD 2.4 billion, up 4% from HKD 2.3 billion in Q4 2022.
We ended 2023 with full year revenue growing 31% to HKD 10 billion. Brokerage commission and handling charge income was HKD 904 million, a decrease of 14% year-over-year and 10% QoQ. The decrease was mainly driven by lower trading volume. Interest income was HKD 1.3 billion, up 17% year-over-year and down 11% QoQ. The year-over-year increase was mainly driven by high interest income from clients' cash deposits due to higher benchmark interest rate and higher margin financing income due to an increase in daily average margin balance. The QoQ decrease was mostly driven by the lower interest income from clients' cash deposits due to decrease in daily average client cash balance.
Other income was HKD 137 million, up 46% year-over-year and largely flat Q over Q. The year-over-year increase was primarily attributed to higher fund distribution income, partially offset by lower enterprise public relations service income and underwriting fee income. Our total costs were HKD 433 million, an increase of 27% from HKD 342 million in Q4 of 2022. Brokerage commission and handling charge expenses were HKD 59 million, down 8% year-over-year and 6% Q over Q. The decrease was roughly in line with our decrease in our brokerage commission and handling charge income, partially offset by the cost of migrating our SGX equities to our self-clearing system. Interest expenses were HKD 271 million, up 49% year-over-year and down 6% quarter-over-quarter.
The year-over-year increase was driven by high interest expenses associated with our security borrowing and the lending business, and the higher margin financing interest expenses. The quarter over quarter decrease was mostly due to lower interest expenses associated with our security borrowing and the lending business, partially offset by high margin financing interest expenses. Processing and servicing costs was HKD 104 million, up 7% year-over-year, and 21% quarter over quarter. The increase was largely due to higher product service fee for new markets and higher system usage fees. As a result, our total gross profit was HKD 1.9 billion, largely flat year-over-year. Gross margin was 81.7% as compared to 85% in Q4 2022. Operating expenses was up 12% year-over-year, and 3% quarter over quarter for HKD 916 million.
R&D expenses was $363 million, up 9% year-over-year, and 1% quarter over quarter. The year-over-year increase was mainly due to increasing R&D head count as we continue to support new product offerings in international markets. Selling and marketing expenses was $182 million, up 19% year-over-year, and down 14% quarter over quarter. The year-over-year increase was due to a 41% year-over-year increase in net new paying clients, partially offset by lower customer acquisition costs. The quarter over quarter decrease was due to few net new clients and the lower customer acquisition costs. G&A expenses was $317 million, up 12% year-over-year, and 15% quarter over quarter. The increase was primarily due to an increase in head count for general administrative personnel, partially offset by lower professional service fees.
As a result, income from operations decreased 9% year-over-year and 22% quarter-over-quarter to HKD 1 billion. Operating margin declined to 43.1% from 49.1% in Q4 2022, mostly due to operating deleverage. Our net income decreased by 9% year-over-year and 20% quarter-over-quarter to HKD 876 million. Net income margin shrank to 36.9% in Q4 as compared to 42% in the same quarter last year. Among our international business, Singapore was the first to achieve break-even on a quarterly basis, even with partial support from headquarters. As client assets continue to grow, we believe the unit economics in Singapore will maintain an upward trajectory. That concludes our prepared remarks. We'd now like to open the call to questions. Operator, please go ahead. Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. To ask a question, you'll need to press star one and one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. To withdraw your question, please press star one and one again. Once again, that's star one and one to ask a question. Please stand by while we compile the Q&A, Russ. Thank you. We'll now take the first question. Please stand by. First question today is from the line of Cindy Wang from China Renaissance. Please go ahead.
Cindy Wang
Analyst and Director, China Renaissance
Thanks for taking my call, and I have two questions. First one is, what's your progress of improving account opening process in Japan? Could you provide more color on new paying clients acquisition in Q4 last year versus Q1 this year so far in Japan? When would you expect to launch Japan stock trading? The second question is regarding to the new paying clients. We see the new paying client target of 350,000 in 2024 is very impressive. Could you break down by key markets, including like Hong Kong, Singapore, US, Japan, et cetera? Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Cindy. I will take your second question first, and we'll leave the first question to my colleague, Daniel. In terms of our new targets for 2024, the contributions from Singapore, Hong Kong, and, you know, Australia in absolute terms should be similar to last year. The incremental growth drivers mainly come from certain new markets we enter into this year and recently in Q4 last year, such as Japan, Canada, and Malaysia. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Hi, Cindy, this is Daniel, and I'll take your question on Japan. In Q4, we continued to optimize the account opening process and to integrate the redundant processes and pages in that process and to iterate on the key friction points. We have seen therefore a very meaningful increase in the conversion rate from users to registered clients to paying clients. In comparison to other international markets, there is still a lot of room for improvement in that conversion number. To continue to optimize that account opening golden process will be a key priority for us this year. In terms of Japan equities trading, yes, we are planning to roll out Japan equities trading to our Japan clients by the end of March.
In April or May, we're gonna roll out Japan equities trading to our clients in Hong Kong and Singapore. Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. We'll now take our next question. This is from the line of Chiyao Huang from Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.
Chiyao Huang
Research Analyst, Morgan Stanley
My question is on the Singapore. So what was roughly the client number and client asset contribution on the overall firm basis? And also wonder what's the strategy in Singapore for 2024, and how is the competitive landscape changing in Singapore? And also what's the, you know, risk appetite evolving for Singapore clients in 2024, given that the US market is still performing quite well? Are they trading more stocks? Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Chiyao. My colleague Robin will answer this question for you.
Robin Xu
SVP, Futu Holdings
Hello.
In Q4, Singapore recorded very steady client growth and contributed about 30% of our total net new clients for the entire quarter. Thanks to the continued net asset inflows of our existing clients and the higher quality new clients, the total client assets and average client assets in Singapore have recorded 25% and 17% sequential growth respectively. The total client assets have reported sequential increase for every single quarter since we launched the business. Average client assets have been on a upward trajectory for 6 consecutive quarters. As of the end of last year, average client assets in Singapore was over 17,000 SGD.
We believe that as we continue to enhance our brand awareness, to diversify and enrich our product offerings, and to improve our client services, Moomoo will continue to attract more high net worth individuals. We've also seen the unit economics in Singapore continue to improve in the past two years. Taking into account the cost from the headquarters to support Singapore, the Singapore subsidiary broke even for the first time during Q4. We have seen very good growth year to date. In terms of clients' risk appetite, during the past rate hike cycle, we started to promote our Cash Plus product, which is the money market fund product. We continue to cross-sell different investment products based on our clients' risk appetite.
This year we have seen very strong traction in US equities among our Singapore clients. Thank you.
Chiyao Huang
Research Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Thank you very much.
You Fan
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, CICC
Thank you. We'll now take our next question. This is from the line of You Fan from CICC. Please go ahead.
好的，谢谢管理层给我这个提问的机会，我是中金公司的分析师樊优。那我这边有两个问题想请教一下，首先第一个的话是关于这个综合的佣金率，那我们看到其实这个季度环比进一步还是有所提升的，想请教一下背后的原因。然后第二个问题是关于这个获客成本，看到其实这个季度整体的获客成本环比也是有比较明显的一个下降，也是想请教一下背后的原因，然后包括咱们后续各个这个新市场继续加大展业之后，怎么去展望未来的一个获客成本趋势。我这边快速翻译一下。My first question is regarding the blended commission rate.
We see the commission rate increase this quarter, so what's the reason behind? The second question is about the CAC. We see the CAC decrease a lot this quarter. What's the reason behind? And how do you view the future trend of the CAC?
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you. I will take these two questions. For commission rate, the combined take rate is almost flat on a QoQ basis, slightly up because of the product mixture and more contributions from our derivative products. Then for the CAC, we further optimize different, you know, marketing campaigns channels to control and even decrease our CAC, which bore very strong results in Q4. Looking forward and based on the year-to-date situations, we do expect this year the CAC number will decrease compared with last year, hopefully, by 10% to 20% year-on-year. Thank you.
You Fan
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, CICC
好的，谢谢，非常清楚。Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. We'll now take our next question. Please stand by. Next question is from the line of Emma Xu from Bank of America Securities. Please go ahead.
Emma Xu
Director and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America Securities
谢谢给我这个提问的机会。我这边也是有两个问题，第一个问题就是刚刚我们重点介绍的新加坡，就是客户的这个质量在持续的改善。那我想问一下，就是说其他的这几个主要的国际市场，我们的客户质量变化是怎样的？就是户均资产有没有也在改善呢？然后包括香港市场的话，随着我们更多地去获取这个线下客户，香港客户这边的……
那个客户画像或者这个整体的资产规模，平均资产规模有没有变化？然后第二个…… 喂，对，能听见吗？然后第二个问题是想问一下关于成交量的。就是，成交量的话，其实在四季度也跌到了一个，换手率也跌到了一个历史的低点。然后香港市场这个成交不活跃其实也比较理解，因为市场情况确实不好，但是美股的话，成交量也，这个看起来成交量也是有一个比较明显的下滑哈。但是其实美股四季度表现还可以，然后包括一季度美股也是有一个持续的很好的表现。所以就想问一下，我们应该去怎样思考这个，换手率和，市场表现的关系。然后一季度的话，我们是否看到了这个，换手率啊，成交量啊，从四季度的低点，有一个明显的反弹呢？
I have two questions. The first one is about the client quality in other international markets. You mentioned earlier about the positive progress in the Singapore client quality, but how about other international markets?
Do you also see improvement in the average client asset? For your Hong Kong market, with you penetrating into the mass market, how will the client profile and average client asset change? The second question is about your trading velocity and trading volume. The trading velocity declined to a record low in Q4, and it is quite understandable that the Hong Kong trading velocity declined due to the weak market. However, US market actually performed quite well in the Q4, but your US trading volume also declined. How should we think about the connection between the market performance and your trading volume and your trading velocity? Do we see a notable rebound of your trading velocity in Q1?
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you. I will take your second question first and leave the first question to my colleague Daniel. In terms of trading velocity, you are right. The trading velocity is down in Hong Kong and the US, in Q4. Despite the US stocks performed very well, in Q4, but it remains a very strong, continuous uptrend, for the whole quarters. Most of our clients actually use a buy-and-hold strategy to enjoy the rallies.
The implied volatility in the US markets, in Q4 actually, went down, compared with Q3. The trading velocities, you know, decrease, actually, you know, based on our humble observations, is in line with a lot of other US discount brokers' operating metrics as well. In the first quarter this year, so far, we have seen a very healthy pickup, not only in the US, but also in Hong Kong in terms of the trading volume and also the trading velocity. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Emma. This is Daniel, and I will take your question on the client quality in international markets.
Actually, we have seen an improvement in average AUM, not only in Singapore, but also in our other international markets, including the US, Australia, and Japan. Mostly because, unlike some of our other peers, I think Futu really cares about quality growth. Net inflow of AUM is a key KPI, very important KPI for all of our marketing teams across different international regions. In Q4, we have seen very strong AUM inflows despite weak market sentiments. In the first two months this year, as Leaf mentioned in his opening remarks, we have a higher net asset inflow in the first two months of this year than the entire Q4 combined. Actually, over one-third of that net asset inflow comes from international markets.
We'll expect a continued upward trajectory in our client assets across international markets. For Hong Kong, in the past couple of quarters, we continued to attract older clients, especially with our offline store. We have seen that these clients typically have higher average assets. Because of the large base effect, these new clients didn't change the overall client profile much in Hong Kong. Thank you.
Emma Xu
Director and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America Securities
Thank you. This is really encouraging.
Operator
Thank you. We'll now take our next question. This is from the line of Leon Qi from Daiwa. Please go ahead.
Leon Qi
Regional Head of Asia Financials, FinTech, and HealthTech Research, Daiwa Capital Markets
好的，非常感谢给我这个提问的机会。我是Leon Qi。有两个问题想请教一下管理层。首先是在我们这个香港的营销策略上，因为刚才讲新加坡讲的比较多了，刚才也听到管理层讲这个新的有资产客户的指引上面，就是明年香港新增的有资产客户是跟这个……
就2024年是跟2023年差不多的。那么随着我们香港现有的这个有资产客户的基数越来越大，不知道管理层会不会这个逐渐把这个业务经营上面的重点，从获客数一点点转向客均资产，就想了解一下这个，管理层在这方面是怎么样打算的。第二个呢是想请教一下我们美股，这个我知道我们技术上已经是可以自清算了，但实际上，是不是美股完全都已经自清算了。我们自清算之后，除了对于我们净利收入的帮助之外，对于我们的这个交易效率，是不是有提高？不知道这方面是不是有一些美国的同业，可以给我们对比，比如说像Interactive Brokers这一些。好，我这个用英文翻译一下。Thanks for taking my questions.
This is Leon Qi. I wanna ask two questions today. Firstly is on our Hong Kong marketing and client acquisition strategy. Just now management shared a lot of details on Singapore, but I'm interested in Hong Kong now. Given we have an increasing number of client base, paying client base now, would management feel that going forward, it will be increasingly more difficult for us to acquire new customers? Are we considering gradually shifting our focus from the number of customers into average AUM or the quality of our customers? We do appreciate the new customer guidance that management talked about just now, that Hong Kong new customers guidance in 2024 would be similar to 2023.
Second question is on self-clearing in US stocks. May I confirm that all of our trades in US has already been self-cleared? In addition to the positive impact on our net interest income, do we see any improvement in terms of our trading execution efficiencies by using self-clearing? Wondering if we can make any comparisons with our competitors in the US such as Interactive Brokers, et cetera. Thank you very much.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Leon. I'll let Lee to take the first question, and I will answer the second one.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
感谢提问。我来回答那个关于香港的问题。香港市场是我们的大本营。2023年我们在香港的年轻人群体当中，持续保持着一个非常高的渗透率。我们在其他年龄段的人口渗透率也在稳步的提升。那么截止到第四季度，富途在香港35到55岁人群中的有资产客户渗透率已经超过了10%。在香港市场，我们的目标是高质量的增长，我们着重获取高质量客户，并且针对存量客户去做精细化的运营。因此在市场行情疲软的时候，我们会在净入金方面依然能看到它是保持着一个非常强劲的势头。未来我们会更好地去利用富途在全品类的优势，去延续对不同的资产量级和投资需求的人群，去做分层运营的策略，并且会持续去关注净入金的趋势。谢谢。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
The Hong Kong market is our home base, and in 2023, we continue to maintain very high penetration among the younger clients. We also steadily improve our penetration into clients from other age groups. As of the end of Q4, our paying client penetration among the adults aged 35 to 55 in Hong Kong was over 10%. In Hong Kong, our goal is to achieve high quality growth, and we focus on acquiring high quality clients and also focus on attracting net asset inflow from existing clients. That's why, during Q4 and also in the past, where market sentiments were weak. We continue to see very robust net asset inflow from Hong Kong. Going forward, we'll leverage our comprehensive product offerings and have different operational strategies for clients with different asset amount and different investment needs.
We'll very closely track the net asset inflow trend in Hong Kong. Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
For the second question, you are right. We have already largely completed the US self-clearing so far. I think actually the positive contributions from this migration will continue thanks to the increase in the client asset cohort and also the contributions from the new markets, such as Japan and Malaysia. In terms of the operating efficiency, definitely, you know, after the self-clearing capabilities, our service downtime versus before has been meaningfully decreased. Also the trading execution in terms of the reporting, et cetera, will be more smooth. Thank you.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
Thank you very much.
Operator
Thank you. As a reminder, if you would like to ask a question, you can press star one and one on your keypad. We will now take our next question. Please stand by. The next question is from the line of Peter Zhang from JPMorgan. Please go ahead.
Peter Zhang
Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan Chase & Co.
谢谢管理层给我提问的问题。
提问的机会。我是摩根大通的Peter。我的第一个问题是关于利息收入，这个季度利息收入环比有所下降。我想请教一下管理层，背后的原因是什么？管理层分别讲解一下客户闲置资金的情况，还有我们利率的一些零存款利率的一个趋势。然后我想问一下，一季度以来我们客户的闲置资金余额的情况的最新的变动趋势是如何的？第二个问题，我是想问一下关于成本端的。我想问一下，管理层对于2024年我们增员的headcount的一个情况，有没有一个指引？然后管理层对于我们2024年成本端的增长，还有成本收入比的一个变化，有没有一个指引？我翻译一下。
Uh, my first question is about interest income. We noticed that interest income had been decreased sequentially in Q1. We wish to understand what's the Q4 trends for clients idle cash and Futu's deposit rates. And I also wish to understand what's the trend in Q1 for clients idle cash balance. My second question is about operating expense. I wish to understand what's Futu's plan for the headcount increase in 2024, and what's management's guidance for Futu's operating expense increase or, say, cost-to-income ratio trend. Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Peter. I will take these two questions. For idle cash, roughly the idle cash accounts for 10% to 15% of our total client assets in the past quarter. The similar situations happened in Q1 so far. The decrease of the interest revenue in Q4, as I mentioned in the opening remarks, is mainly due to the decrease of the average balance for the security borrowing and the lending. Despite if you see the balance sheet data, the margin and the security lending balance was higher than that in Q3. For the second half of your questions, in terms of headcount, we are looking for mid- to high-single-digit headcount growth.
Mainly, we'll be deployed for our international market expansion and to further enhance our R&D capabilities. Unfortunately, we do not have a cost-income ratio guidance. Given the nature of our business, our revenue is very volatile, is very difficult to predict due to the market volatility. We were more focusing on the people side, given this is one of the largest, you know, cost components for our overall cost structure. Thank you.
Peter Zhang
Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan Chase & Co.
谢谢，非常清楚。Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. This does conclude the question and answer session. At this time, I would like to hand the conference back to Daniel Yuan for closing remarks. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
That concludes our call today. On behalf of the Futu management team, I would like to thank you for joining us today. If you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact me or any of our investor relations representatives. Thank you and goodbye.
Operator
Thank you. This does conclude today's conference call. Thank you for participating, and you may now disconnect.

content.text:
Operator
Hello, ladies and gentlemen. Welcome to Futu Holdings Third Quarter 2023 Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After management's prepared remarks, there will be a Q&A session. Today's conference call is being recorded. If you have any objections, you may disconnect at this time. I would now like to turn the conference over to your host for today's conference call, Daniel Yuan, Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR at Futu. Please go ahead.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Thanks, operator, and thank you for joining us today to discuss our third quarter 2023 earnings results. Joining me on the call today are Mr. Leaf Li, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Arthur Chen, Chief Financial Officer, and Robin Xu, Senior Vice President. As a reminder, today's call may include forward-looking statements, which represent the company's belief regarding future events, which by their nature are not certain and are outside of the company's control. Forward-looking statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties. We caution you that a number of important factors could cause actual results to differ materially from those containing any forward-looking statements. For more information about the potential risks and uncertainties, please refer to the company's filings with the SEC, including its annual report on Form 20-F. With that, I will now turn the call over to Leaf.
Leaf will make his comments in Chinese, and I will translate.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
三季度我们增加了约6.5万名有资产客户，环比增长12%。有资产客户总数达到165万，同比增长14%。2023年前三个季度，我们获得了超过16.3万名有资产客户，已经高于年初时给出的全年获客指引。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Thank you all for joining today. In the third quarter, we acquired around 65,000 paying clients, a 12% sequential increase. Our total paying clients reached 1.65 million, a 14% year-over-year. Three quarters into 2023, we have exceeded our full year guidance by acquiring over 163,000 paying clients.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
三季度，香港市场为我们贡献了超过40%的净增有资产客户。七月份，股市经历了短暂的反弹，刺激了客户的入市情绪，获客速度也有所提升。八九月份，我们围绕政府绿债和银债的发行进行了有效的市场推广，进一步帮助我们吸引了许多资产配置导向的客户。七月底，我们在香港的第一家实体店正式开业。在实体店内，我们的工作人员协助客户进行开户，向客户演示产品的高阶功能，并回答客户对我们产品的疑问。实体店帮助我们提升了在香港市场的品牌认知，并以较低的获客成本吸引中老年人群体。三季度，55岁及以上的客户占实体店新增有资产客户的一半以上。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
In the third quarter, Hong Kong market contributed over 40% of new paying clients. This acceleration in client acquisition was driven by the relief rally in the first half of the quarter, and successful marketing around the government's green bond and silver bond issuances in the second half. These two bond offerings attracted allocation-driven clients to our platform. In late July, we opened the first offline store in Hong Kong to raise brand awareness, assist clients with account opening, demonstrate advanced product features, and address inquiries regarding our products and services. Through this offline store, we managed to attract middle-aged and senior clients at a lower customer acquisition cost. In fact, clients aged 55 and above contributed over 50% of paying clients acquired through the offline store in the third quarter.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
在新加坡，我们围绕现金管理产品Cash Plus推出了一系列营销活动，取得了不错的效果。季度末，有资产客户数同比增长35%。在美国，随着新增有资产客户的净入资环比增长，客户质量进一步得到改善。九月份，我们在日本和加拿大正式上线了证券经纪业务，目前为日本客户提供美股的交易服务，为加拿大客户提供美股和加股的交易服务。在新市场展业初期，我们会把重心放在打磨开户入金的黄金流程，完善交易产品能力，以及不断优化品牌定位和迭代营销策略上。尽管全球股市表现疲软，我们的季度有资产客户留存率仍然保持在98%以上。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
In Singapore, we launched successful marketing campaigns to promote our cash management product Cash Plus, thereby growing our paying clients by 35% year-over-year. We continue to observe improvement in client quality in the U.S. as net asset inflow of new paying clients trended higher. In September, we officially launched our brokerage business in Japan and Canada, now offering clients access to U.S. stock trading in Japan, and U.S. and Canadian stock trading in Canada. During the early innings of market launch, we will remain focused on refining our account opening onboarding process, expanding trading products, and honing our brand positioning and marketing messages. Despite bearish sentiments across global equity markets, we recorded another quarter of over 98% paying client retention rate.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
我们持续在各个市场扩充交易产品品类。在新加坡，我们上线了碎股功能，为新手投资者降低了美股的投资门槛。在香港和美国，我们优化了期权交易能力，为活跃期权交易者推出组合期权移仓功能，支持期权交易者将即将到期的期权合约以不同的到期日和执行价进行移仓，这大大提升了期权策略的灵活度。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
We continue to enrich trading product offerings across markets. In Singapore, we launched fractional shares for U.S. stocks and ETFs to enhance accessibility for novice investors. We optimized our product for active options traders by introducing multi-leg options rollover strategy in Hong Kong and the U.S. This trading function gives options traders flexibility to roll contracts near expiration to a later date at different strike prices.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
客户总资产达到4,680亿港币，同比增长27%。尽管市场回撤对客户持仓市值带来了负面影响，得益于强劲的客户净入金，客户总资产环比仍保持稳定。值得一提的是，随着新增客户质量的不断提高，新加坡客户的总资产连续第五个季度实现了双位数的环比增长。和上季度获取的有资产客户相比，本季度新加坡新增有资产客户的户均资产额环比增长了20%。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Total client assets increased by 27% year-over-year to HKD 468 billion. While the market pullback drags the valuation of our client stock holdings, total client assets remain stable quarter over quarter due to robust net asset inflow. Notably, total client assets in Singapore achieved double-digit sequential growth for the fifth consecutive quarter, which was partially driven by higher new asset quality. The average asset balance of new paying clients in Singapore was 20% higher than the prior quarter. Trading volume in Q3 rebounded as clients traded more actively amid heightened volatility. Total trading volume increased by 14% sequentially to HKD 1.1 trillion, of which U.S. stock trading constituted around 75%. Higher trading turnover of the Magnificent Seven stocks led U.S. stock trading volume to grow by 19% quarter over quarter.
Hong Kong stock trading volume increased by 5% sequentially, mainly driven by rising trading interest in leveraged and inverse ETFs. Margin financing and securities lending balance slipped 4% quarter-over-quarter as some clients unwound their bets against popular U.S. technology names. Total client assets under management grew to HKD 52 billion as of quarter-end, up 100% year-over-year and 19% quarter-over-quarter. In the third quarter, client assets in bonds increased by 87% sequentially as U.S. Treasury bills maintained high yields. In Hong Kong, structured notes were met with high demand from high-net-worth clients as their risk appetite abated amid macro uncertainties. As a result, private loan balance grew by 52% quarter-over-quarter.
In Singapore, total client assets and wealth management increased by five-fold year-over-year, driven by tripling of wealth management clients and higher average asset balance. In the third quarter, we further expanded our product portfolio in Singapore by introducing structured notes and SGS bonds. We have 391 IPO distribution and IR clients as of quarter end, up 30% year-over-year. In the third quarter, we acted as joint bookrunners of several high-profile Hong Kong IPOs, including those of TUHU Car, 4Paradigm, and Keep. We also participated in the Hong Kong IPOs of all companies with market capitalization over HKD 10 billion by the end of quarter. In the first three quarters, we underwrote 26 Hong Kong IPOs and ranked first among all Hong Kong brokers, according to Wind. Next, I'd like to invite our CFO, Arthur, to discuss our financial performance.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Leaf and Daniel. Now, please allow me to walk you through our financial performance in the third quarter. All the numbers are in Hong Kong dollar unless otherwise noted. Total revenue was HKD 2.7 billion, up 36% from HKD 1.9 billion in Q3 2022. Brokerage commission and the handling charge income was HKD 1 billion, an increase of 5% year-over-year and 6% Q-over-Q. Higher contributions from derivative trading lift the blended commission rate from 8.8 basis points in the third quarter last year to 9.3 basis points this quarter. Interest income was HKD 1.5 billion, an increase of 71% year-over-year and 7% Q-over-Q. The sequential increase was mainly driven by higher interest rates on clients' cash deposits, partially offset by lower cash balance.
Other income was HKD 137 million, up 28% year-over-year and 8% Q-over-Q. The increase was largely due to higher fund distribution income. Our total costs were HKD 437 million, an increase of 101% from HKD 218 million in Q3 2022. Brokerage commission and the handling charge expenses were HKD 63 million, down 24% year-over-year and up 14% Q-over-Q. The expenses didn't move in tandem with brokerage commission and handling charge income, mainly due to cost saving from our U.S. self-clearing business. Interest expenses were HKD 289 million, up 546% year-over-year and 31% Q-over-Q. The year-over-year and the Q-over-Q increase were both driven by higher interest expenses associated with our securities lending business.
Processing and servicing costs were HKD 86 million, down 6% year-over-year and 13% Q-over-Q. The year-over-year decrease was mainly due to savings from cloud service fee as a result of system optimization, and the Q-over-Q decrease was mainly due to lower system usage fee. As a result, total gross profit was HKD 2.2 billion, an increase of 28% from HKD 1.7 billion in Q3 2022. Gross margin was 84% as compared with 89% in the third quarter of 2022. Operating expenses was up 17% year-over-year and 5% Q-over-Q to HKD 893 million. R&D expenses were HKD 360 million, up 15% year-over-year and down marginally by 1% Q-over-Q.
The year-over-year increase was mainly due to higher R&D headcount as we continue to upgrade our infrastructure, roll out new products and features, and customize products for international markets. Selling and marketing expenses was HKD 212 million, down 10% year-over-year and up 21% Q-over-Q. The expenses declined year-over-year due to lower customer acquisition costs, and the Q-over-Q increase was primarily driven by accelerated paying client growth. General and administrative expenses were HKD 322 million, up 52% year-over-year and 3% Q-over-Q. The rise was primarily due to an increase in headcount for general administrative personnel to support our international markets.
As a result, our net income increased by 45% year-over-year and it declined by 3% Q-over-Q to HKD 1.1 billion. Net income margin expanded to 41% from 39% in the same quarter last year, mainly due to strong revenue growth and the lower selling and marketing expenses. That concludes our prepared remarks. We'd now like to open the call to questions. Operator, please go ahead.
Operator
The first question comes from the line of Leon Qi with Daiwa. Please go ahead.
Leon Qi
Head of Asia Financials, FinTech and HealthTech Research, Daiwa
Hi. Thanks for taking my question. Thanks, management, for taking my questions. This is Leon from Daiwa. My first question is regarding our new market, especially in Japan. We understand we just launched in Japan in late September. I'm interested in the user behavior in terms of our Japan new clients. Does management see any early indicators in terms of the trading velocity, [uncertain] penetration, and the specific trading products that our Japanese clients are being engaged in. If there are any significant differences in terms of I'm these metrics for customers in Japan versus other markets.
Also I'm Interested to know the customer acquisition cost for us in Japan. Appreciate any color on the unit economics in Japan. My second question is on wealth management. We do appreciate the very rapid growth of our AUM in wealth management. Per management introduction just now, money market fund is a major reason behind that. I'm sure this is partly because of the high U.S. interest rates, but if we look at it from an across interest rate cycle perspective, how much proportion does management expect the non-money market fund products to contribute in our overall wealth management AUM?
Also what is our take rate on money market fund now? Thank you very much.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Leon. Let my colleague Daniel answer the first question first, and I will answer the second question. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Sure.
Unfortunately, we now only offer U.S. cash equities trading to our Japanese clients. It's, you know, we don't have margin, we don't have Japanese stock trading, so we only have data for client behavior on U.S. stock trading. So far, the turnover of U.S. stock trading is not so different from what we've seen in other markets. That being said, we have a very aggressive and ambitious product roadmap for next year, and some of the products that I mentioned that we don't support now will be rolled out in the next couple of quarters. In terms of client acquisition cost, because we're coming from a small base of clients, whereas we have a lot of fixed costs for like setting up markets, setting up like offices in Japan, and hiring marketing personnel.
Obviously our CAC for this quarter and next quarter in Japan will be higher than our group average. Over time, as we increase the number of clients in Japan, the CAC will gradually come down. So far, we have no reason to believe that the CAC in Japan will be higher than what we've seen in other markets. Just to give you some other colors and updates on our Japan business, we now have slightly over 400,000 users on our platform. Overall users have been very active, and we observe that on average during the trading days, our DAU to user ratio is close to 20%, which is the highest among all the markets we are currently in.
User growth along with paying client growth will be our key priorities for next year. Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Okay. For second question regarding the wealth manager, I think the key for us to do this kind of business is to engage the client and, focus on the long-term values of the clients. Therefore, we do not put too emphasis on the near-term, monetizations. Having said that, the take rate for these, you know, money market funds is, essentially just similar to our other products, such as equity products or fixed income products. I think, you know, we have already established a very comprehensive matrix, in terms of the product offerings, in our, for instance, besides the money market fund, we also have the equity products, fixed income products.
In particular, as Leaf mentioned in the opening remarks, we have launched free floating interest- floating rate-- No. FCN products, in the past two quarters and recorded a very strong growth. We think these products will further diversify our clients' asset allocations, and help them to navigate different interest cycles down the line.
Leon Qi
Head of Asia Financials, FinTech and HealthTech Research, Daiwa
Thank you very much for your color, Arthur and Daniel.
Operator
Thank you. Next question comes from the line of Chiyao Huang with MS. Please go ahead.
Chiyao Huang
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
The first question is on the idle cash, and we saw some sequential decline in idle cash. Just wondering what's the reason for that, and if we are seeing some of the existing clients are shifting their cash to mutual funds or other products. Also a related question is for the new inflow of our clients, what's roughly the proportion between stocks and other investment products such as mutual funds? Second question is, can management talk about the strategy in Japan as we are seeing some local brokers are offering zero commission already. What's our competitive strategy there? What's the thinking about the future monetization? Would we be considering, you know, building more comprehensive financial offerings and capabilities in Japan in order to improve the monetization over time?
Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
In terms of your first question, the idle cash decrease was primarily due to our clients shift their cash positions to more equities, stocks, especially on the U.S. stocks, assets, at the quarter end. Also the partial reason is because, you know, some clients allocated more on the wealth management products, during the quarter end as well. In terms of the new clients' inflows, the allocations among cash, stock, and also the wealth management, roughly, you know, stock positions account for 70% and the wealth management products account for 10% and the remaining belongs to the idle cash. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan

The year-over-year decrease was mainly due to savings from cloud service fee as a result of system optimization, and the Q-over-Q decrease was mainly due to lower system usage fee. As a result, total gross profit was HKD 2.2 billion, an increase of 28% from HKD 1.7 billion in Q3 2022. Gross margin was 84% as compared with 89% in Q3 2022. Operating expenses was up 17% year-over-year and 5% Q-over-Q to HKD 893 million. R&D expenses were HKD 360 million, up 15% year-over-year and down marginally by 1% Q-over-Q.
The year-over-year increase was mainly due to higher R&D headcount as we continue to upgrade our infrastructure, roll out new products and features, and customize products for international markets. Selling and marketing expenses was HKD 212 million, down 10% year-over-year and up 21% Q-over-Q. The expenses declined year-over-year due to lower customer acquisition costs, and the Q-over-Q increase was primarily driven by accelerated paying client growth. General and administrative expenses were HKD 322 million, up 52% year-over-year and 3% Q-over-Q. The rise was primarily due to an increase in headcount for general administrative personnel to support our international markets. As a result, our net income increased by 45% year-over-year, and it declined by 3% Q-over-Q to HKD 1.1 billion.
Net income margin expanded to 41% from 39% in the same quarter last year, mainly due to strong revenue growth and the lower selling and marketing expenses. That concludes our prepared remarks. We'd now like to open the call to questions. Operator, please go ahead.
Operator
Thank you. If you wish to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. If you wish to cancel your request, please press star two. If you are on a speakerphone, please pick up your handset to ask your question. The first question comes from the line of Leon Qi with Daiwa. Please go ahead.
Leon Qi
Head of Asia Financials, FinTech and HealthTech Research, Daiwa
Hi. Thanks for taking my question.
想请教管理层两个问题。第一是我们这个新市场，刚才管理层也讲到了，我们展业的两个新市场，日本和加拿大，那特别是在日本这一边，虽然说时间还比较短，我不知道我们管理层有没有观察到一些这个early indicator，比如说在我们的客户行为上面，他们的这个交易频率，他们take margin的这个比例，他们去交易的这些具体产品，不知道和我们在其他市场的这个客户，这些客户行为是不是有不同？另外呢，就是我们获客成本上面，这个有没有什么不同？这个unit economics，麻烦管理层跟我们介绍一下。那另一个呢，就是关于我们的财富管理这一边，当然我们也看到这个AUM的增长是非常迅速，管理层刚才讲到，这个获客可能是增长的一个比较主要的因素。那当然在现在的这个美元利率环境之下，我们也可以理解，获客增速比较高。那当然如果展望得稍微长一点，就是我们这个cross整个interest rate cycle里面，可能管理层觉得是哪一类型的产品，除了获客之外，非获客产品能够占到多大比例吧？以及想了解一下我们现在获客的这个take rate，大概是怎么样的水平。好，那我用英文翻译一下。Thanks management for taking my questions.
This is Leon from Daiwa. My first question is regarding our new markets, especially in Japan. We understand we just launched Japan in late September. I'm interested in the user behavior in terms of our Japanese new clients. Does management see any early indicators in terms of the trading velocities, margin lending penetration and the specific trading products that our Japanese clients are being engaged in? Is there any significant differences in terms of these metrics for customers in Japan versus other markets? Also I'm interested to know the customer acquisition cost for us in Japan. Appreciate any color on the unit economics in Japan. My second question is on wealth management. We do appreciate the very rapid growth of our AUM in wealth management.
Per management introduction just now, money market fund is a major reason behind that. I'm sure this is partly because of the high U.S. interest rates. If we look at it from an across the interest rate cycle perspective, how much proportion does management expect the non-money market fund products to contribute in our overall wealth management AUM? Also, what is our take rate on money market fund now? Thank you very much.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Leon. Let my colleague Daniel answer the first question first, and I will answer the second question. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Sure. Unfortunately, we now only offer U.S. cash equities trading to our Japanese clients. As you know, we don't have margin, we don't have Japanese stock trading, so we only have data for client behavior on U.S. stock trading. So far, the turnover of the U.S. stock trading is not so different from what we've seen in other markets. That being said, we have a very aggressive and ambitious product roadmap for next year, and some of the products that I mentioned that we don't support now will be rolled out in the next couple of quarters. In terms of client acquisition cost, because we're coming from a small base of clients, whereas we have a lot of fixed costs for like setting up markets, setting up like offices in Japan, and hiring marketing personnel.
Obviously our CAC for this quarter and next quarter in Japan will be higher than our group average. Over time, as we increase the number of clients in Japan, the CAC will gradually come down. So far, we have no reason to believe that the CAC in Japan will be higher than what we've seen in other markets. Just to give you some other colors and updates on our Japan business, we now have slightly over 400,000 users on our platform. Overall users have been very active. We observed that on average during the trading days, our DAU to user ratio was close to 20%, which is the highest among all the markets we are currently in.
User growth along with paying client growth will be our key priorities for next year. Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Okay. For second question regarding the wealth management, I think the key for us to do this kind of business is to engage the client and, focus on the long-term values of the clients. Therefore, we do not put too much emphasis on the near-term, monetizations. Having said that, the take rate for these, you know, money market funds is, essentially just similar to our other products, such as equity products or fixed income products. I think, you know, we have already established a very comprehensive matrix, in terms of the product offerings, for instance, besides the money market fund, we also have the equity products, fixed income products.
In particular, as Leaf mentioned in the opening remarks, we have launched FCN products in the past two quarters and recorded a very strong growth. We think these products will further diversify our clients' asset allocations, and help them to navigate different interest cycles down the line.
Leon Qi
Head of Asia Financials, FinTech and HealthTech Research, Daiwa
Thank you very much for your color, Arthur and Daniel.
Operator
Thank you. Next question comes from the line of Chiyao Huang with MS. Please go ahead.
Chiyao Huang
Analyst, Morgan Stanley
感谢冠霖给我提问的机会。我有两个问题想请教冠霖。第一个是关于这个，刚才冠霖也提到这个 idle cash 环比有所减少，想请问这主要的原因是什么？咱们是否看到这个客户有一些存量的资金，他逐渐从这个 cash 放去了一些货币基金等等一些产品。另外跟着想请教一下，这个咱们新的这个客户的入金里面的这个比例，放在股票和这个基金大概是一个什么样的比例？这是第一个问题。第二个问题想请冠霖大概地谈一下这个，因为我们看到日本市场现在基本上也是最近进入了这个零佣金的时代，所以这个从下个季度开始，咱们可能从明年，明年初开始推出这个日股之后，怎么去面对这么样……
去设计自己的这个策略，去应对这样的一个竞争环境，以及长期来看，从去monetize的角度来想的话，我们还有哪些别的一些办法？会否会考虑在日本再发展一些别的一些这种monetize的能力，包括这个财富管理、资产管理，或者是一些trading，或者是外汇等等这些相关的能力。这是第二个问题。谢谢。然后我简单地翻译一下。The first question is on the idle cash, and we saw some sequential decline in idle cash.
Just wondering what's the reason for that? If we are seeing some of the existing clients are shifting their cash to mutual funds or other products. Also a related question is, for the new inflow of our client AUM, what's roughly the proportion between stocks and other investment products such as mutual funds? Second question is, can management talk about the strategy in Japan as we are seeing some local brokers are offering zero commission already. What's our competitive strategy there? What's the thinking about the future monetization? Would we be considering, you know, building more comprehensive financial offerings and capabilities in Japan in order to improve the monetization over time? Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
好的，我来回答第一个问题，然后第二个问题由我的同事Daniel来回答。那，有关我们这个季度的闲置资金占比下降的原因，主要是因为客户在本季度买入了比较多的一些股票的一些资产，特别是美股的资产，在这个季度末的那个时间。那么少量的这个资金呢，也是因为购买基金而减少的。那Chiyao你刚才问到的这个，大概我们新的客户进来的资产的配置呢，大概在股票的仓位大概在70%左右，财富管理的仓位大概在10%左右，那么剩余的大概有20%左右是配置在闲置的资金的。In terms of your first question, the idle cash decrease was primarily due to our clients' shift of their cash positions to more equities, stocks, especially on the U.S. stock assets, at quarter end.
Also the partial reason is because, you know, some clients allocated more on the wealth management products during the quarter end as well. In terms of the new clients' inflows, the allocations among cash, stock, and also the wealth management largely, you know, stock positions account for 70% and the wealth management products account for 10% and the remaining belongs to the idle cash. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Chiyao, I'll take your second question on our monetization strategy in Japan. Yes, as you mentioned, we have seen a couple leading brokers in Japan gone to zero commission for Japanese stock trade. We have reasons to believe that other brokers in Japan will probably follow suit. While no one's gonna make money from Japanese equities trading, U.S. stock trading is still quite profitable. SBI and Rakuten, for example, charge $0.45 for U.S. stock trading. We tend to price more aggressively than these incumbents, but we still expect to make very decent margin on U.S. stock trading. As of the end of last year, we have seen that there are 2.3 million U.S. stock investors in Japan. That's relatively low compared to Japanese stock investors, but that has been growing pretty fast.
As of the end of 2019, there were about 1 million U.S. stock investors. Over the past 4 years it has more than doubled. Besides U.S. stock trading commission, we also intend to monetize over margin financing and foreign exchange fees. We observe that Japanese investors really like to trade on margin. We have seen that in the industry average number, like around 50% of their trades are placed with margin. That's gonna be a key revenue driver. For FX charges, we understand that in order to compensate for zero commission for Japanese stock trading, all of the brokers in Japan charge pretty hefty fees for FX.
As the trading volume of U.S. stock trading on our platform grows, we also expect FX revenue to make a meaningful contribution. Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you very much.
Operator
Thank you. Next question comes from the line of Cindy Wang with China Renaissance. Please go ahead.
Cindy Wang
Analyst, China Renaissance
Hi. Thanks for taking my question. I have two questions. First one is related to Japan market. Can you share the coverage of Japan's maintaining clients' progress? What's the conversion rate from registered users to paying clients? Have you seen maintaining clients increasing month-over-month? Second question is for the PantherTrade applying for digital assets trading platform in Hong Kong. What is the progress with that? What is your preparation work for digital assets trading platform? Would you be able to launch trading functions immediately once their license is approved? Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Cindy. I will answer your second question first, and my colleague Daniel will answer your question regarding Japan. We echo the Web3 policies advocated by the Hong Kong government, who want to build up Hong Kong as a Web3 global center. In the past several quarters, we carefully studied the policies and the regulations issued by Hong Kong SFC.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
PantherTrade, a wholly subsidiary within Futu Group, submitted that VASP license application to Hong Kong SFC last month, and we expect the whole application process may take at least six to nine months, when if we have the luck to get approval in principle. We have not formed a very concrete business plans afterwards, and we will continue to modify this content in the next couple of quarters, and hopefully we can give some new updates in next Q2 or Q3. Thank you.
谢谢Cindy。我来take第一个关于日本的问题。那目前在日本市场，我们从用户到开户客户，然后从开户客户到入金客户的转化率都要比我们其他的国际市场要低一些。那我们觉得主要目前有两个原因吧。第一个原因是可能在我们的开户的这个黄金流程上，我们觉得还是有一些friction points的。那因为目前在日本证券行业的中后台还是涉及了不少体验参差的一些外包的系统，那我们为了尽快可以给客户提供这个开户的能力，其实采用了一些行业通行的一些安排，那这个对用户体验是有一定的负面影响的。那我们未来一段时间会重点去优化开户入金的这个黄金流程，然后在之后几个季度逐渐将这个流程中的一些外包的环节替代为我们自研的这个系统。那另外一个我们觉得造成这个转化率偏低的原因是，就是我们品类上的一些缺失吧。那目前像刚才提到的只上线了美股正股的交易，那我们预计明年一季度可以上线日股的交易和这个NISA账户的能力。那虽然我们相信富途的这个美股交易能力在日本的市场中是遥遥领先的，但是目前在日本，日股依旧是本地投资者非常重要的一个交易的标的。那我们是希望我们之后在当地市场推广的时候，品类也是比较完善的。所以根据我们对目前用户的一些调研，我们理解这个也是阻碍部分用户在我们这开户入金的一个原因吧。
I'm gonna translate for myself. Right now in Japan, the user to client conversion rate as well as the client to paying client conversion rate are both lower than what we have observed in other international markets. We think there are two main reasons behind it. Number one is that our account opening onboarding process still has a number of friction points. So far, the mid- to back-office in the Japanese brokerage industry are still characterized by a lot of outsourced systems that have really unsatisfactory user experience. In order to start account opening soon, we leverage some of these outsourced systems, which really have a negative impact on our users' experience, and thus impacted the conversion rate from account opening to asset deposits. In next couple of quarters, we plan to invest into our account opening process and gradually replace these outsourced systems with our proprietary system. The second reason behind this low conversion rate so far is the lack of key trading products. As mentioned earlier, we now only offer U.S. cash equities trading to Japan users. In Q1 next year, we plan to launch Japanese stock trading as well as NISA account. Although we are really confident that Futu's U.S. stock trading capabilities lead our Japanese peers by a very wide margin. In Japan, the Japanese stock investing is still very, very popular. We understand based on our user survey that lack of, you know, Japanese equity trading is a key reason that prevents them from opening accounts with us. Thank you.
Operator
Ms. Wang, are you done with your question?
Cindy Wang
Analyst, China Renaissance
Yes.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Yes, I am done, thank you.
Cindy Wang
Analyst, China Renaissance
It's okay. Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. A reminder to all the participants that you may press star and one to ask a question. Next question comes from the line of Peter Zhang with JP Morgan. Please go ahead.
Peter Zhang
Analyst, JPMorgan
谢谢管理层给我提供的机会。我对于日本这边我还是有一个follow-up的问题，我想问一下，在未来有没有机会，就是我们香港或者新加坡的用户可以去交易日股，就是在我们的product pipeline上有没有这个考虑？然后第二个问题是，就是这个季度交易的那个佣金费率环比有所下降，我想问一下背后的原因以及未来的趋势会如何？
Okay, let me do the translation. My first question is a follow-up question regarding the Japan product line. I wish to understand, going forward, will Futu's clients in Hong Kong or Singapore market be allowed to trade Japan stock? Is this product in your product pipeline? My second question is regarding the blended commission fee rate. We notice that the blended commission fee rate declined sequentially in Q3, and we wish to understand what's the reason behind, and what will be the trend going forward. Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
好的，谢谢 Peter。我来回答你的这两个问题。第一个是有关这个日本的股票交易会不会这个功能在其他的这些市场里面提供。那我们的答案是确定的，而且这已经在我们的相应的产品排期的相应的一个管线里面。我相信这个对于日本以外的其他的一些交易者的获取，包括他们的留存，以及对于我们的收入，都会有一个非常正面的帮助。
那么第二个问题有关于我们三季度的佣金费率环比的小幅下降，这个原因呢，我们在之前其实好几个季度也有解释过，主要的原因是我们的美股交易的收费，是有两种不同的收费套餐，一种呢是按照百分比来收取，还有一种呢是按照股票的数量来收取。所以呢，客户在每个季度交易的股票的面值，交易的大面值的股票跟小面值股票的一个比例，会影响到我们综合的佣金费率，影响在这个里面。所以这个季度的佣金费率环比的小幅下降，也是因为市场的原因在这个里面。那么展望未来的情况，我们目前对于整体的综合佣金费率的稳定，还是保持一个比较乐观的状态。Regarding two questions.
Number one is for the Japan stock trading offering to the markets outside of Japan. Our answer is definitely it would be a yes and has already been in our product pipelines. Hopefully we can launch the U.S., the Japan stock trading to our clients in Hong Kong and Singapore in the near future. We do think this kind of product offering will further helpful to our client engagement in these markets and also increase the clients participation in our platform. Our top line will also benefit arising from that.
Regarding the blended commission rate fluctuation, as we elaborate to the market several quarters, it is mainly due to the clients' trading behaviors, because our U.S. stock trading commissions do have different menus, price menus, and one menu is actually not based on the percentage of the trading volume, but on the number of the shares. When people trade these big blue chips or these, you know, OTC stocks, the combination will have the implications on the blended commission rate as well. In the third quarter, the fluctuation is mainly because of that. Going forward, we think, you know, the blended commission rate if we take out this trading patterns reasons can maintain stable in the near future. Thank you.
Peter Zhang
Analyst, JPMorgan
谢谢，非常非常非常感谢。
Operator
Thank you. Next question comes from the line of Li Wan with BOCOM International. Please go ahead.
Li Wan
Analyst, BOCOM International
感谢给我提问的机会。我想请教一个关于利息收入的问题。就是整个今年您收入的增长，利息收入贡献比较大，那能否给我们拆解一下，比如说融资融券和银行存款的贡献都分别是多少？然后如果明年美联储降息的话，会对我们收入的增速是一个怎样的影响？我翻译一下。Can you give us a breakdown of interest income and what will be the impact from Fed's rate cut next year?
Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
好的，有关利息收入的这个问题我来回答一下。整体我们的这个利息收入里面，客户的闲置资金的这个利息收入的占比，贡献在今年的这个占比贡献是要高于融资融券的，这个利息的收入。那么往前看，我们觉得整个的美联储减息的速度会是一个非常缓慢的状态。那么同时呢，在美联储减息的时候，虽然我们的利息收入会受到一定负面的影响，但是联储的这个减息在同一个情况下也会刺激整体的资本市场的活跃程度。那从以往去看，在减息的这个周期里面，客户参与市场的交易活跃度，包括交易量，都会有相应的上升。在一定程度上，交易收入的上升会弥补掉我们客户的闲置利息收入的下降。 In terms of the interest income, the interest revenues contributed from the client idle cash is much bigger than the interest income derived from the margin lending and the security lending business. Going forward, we do not think the Fed's rate cut will be very fast. In circumstances when the rate cut normally it would be helpful to the trading volumes for the whole capital markets, for our clients as well. Therefore, we do think the trading revenues arising from this rate cut will largely offset the potential idle cash revenue decrease. Thank you.
Operator
Ms. Wan, are you done with your question?
Li Wan
Analyst, BOCOM International
Yes, thank you.
Operator
Thank you. Next question comes from the line of Emma Xu with BofA Securities. Please go ahead. Miss Emma Xu, can you go ahead with your question?
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Well, it seems that Emma is not here tonight. Operator, do you have any further questions on the line?
Operator
There are no more questions. I will now hand the call back over to Mr. Yuan for closing comments. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Sure. Yeah. That concludes our call today. On behalf of the Futu management team, I would like to thank you for joining us today. If you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact me or any of our investor relations representatives. Thank you, and goodbye.
Operator
Thank you. This concludes our conference for today. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.

content.text:
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu
Thanks, operator, and thank you for joining us today to discuss our Q2 2023 earnings results. Joining me on the call today are Mr. Leaf Li, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Arthur Chen, Chief Financial Officer, and Robin Xu, Senior Vice President. As a reminder, today's call may include forward-looking statements, which represent the company's belief regarding future events, which, by their nature, are not certain and are outside of the company's control. Forward-looking statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties. We caution you that a number of important factors could cause actual results to differ materially from those contained in any forward-looking statements. For more information about the potential risks and uncertainties, please refer to the company's filings with the SEC, including its annual report on Form 20-F. With that, I will now turn the call over to Leaf.
Leaf will make his comments in Chinese, and I will translate.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu
[Foreign language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu
Thank you all for joining today. I'm pleased to announce that we acquired over 57,000 paying clients in the Q2, bringing the total number of our paying clients to nearly 1.6 million. Robust organic growth across all overseas markets drove a 41% sequential acceleration in client acquisition. In the Q2, Hong Kong market contributed approximately 1/3 of new paying clients as effective offline marketing campaigns attracted older clients who prefer in-person instructions on how to open trading accounts and navigate our user interface. In Singapore market, we also witnessed strong paying client growth on the back of US equity market outperformance and the enticing yield of money market funds. In the US, we brought in more clients of higher quality as we iterated on marketing channels and client incentives.
Despite fragile market sentiments, our group's quarterly paying client retention rate remained above 98%.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu
[Foreign language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu
In Q2, we continued to roll out new products and features across markets. To help clients better execute their trading strategy, we launched bracket orders for US and Hong Kong stock options and futures and algorithmic orders for all clients in Hong Kong and Singapore. In Singapore and Australia, we now give clients access to certain US stocks and ETFs 24 hours a day, five days a week, thereby enhancing the accessibility of US stock trading.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu
[Foreign language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu
Total client assets were HKD 466 billion. That's 8% year-over-year and flattish quarter-over-quarter. Negative mark-to-market impact on clients' Hong Kong stock holdings dragged total client assets. The net asset inflow in overseas markets remained robust, which offset the market impact. Singapore market delivered strong asset growth during Q2, with a 21% and 12% quarter-over-quarter increase in total and average client assets, respectively. This was the fourth consecutive quarter where the Singapore market achieved double-digit sequential growth in total client assets. Margin financing and securities lending balance declined marginally by 1.4% sequentially as some clients unwound their securities lending position.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu
[Foreign language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu
Total trading volume declined 22% quarter over quarter to HKD 1 trillion. Hong Kong stock trading volume was HKD 259 billion, down 31% sequentially due to clients' waning interest in China technology names, given disappointing stock price performance. US stock trading volume was down by 18% quarter over quarter to HKD 676 billion as trading turnover of technology stocks, leveraged and inverse ETFs contracted.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu
[Foreign language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu
Total client assets under management were HKD 43 billion, up 99% year-over-year and 17% quarter-over-quarter. The sustained high yields of money market funds were the key driver behind this robust asset growth. In Hong Kong, we continue to expand structured product offerings by onboarding fund-linked notes and call spread notes to cater to the diversified risk-return expectations of high net worth clients. In Singapore, over 18% of clients held wealth management positions as of quarter-end, up significantly from 2% in the year-ago quarter. In Singapore, average client assets in wealth management more than doubled year-over-year. In an effort to expand beyond retail wealth management, we launched entrusted accounts in Singapore that allow fund managers to manage assets on their clients' behalf.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu
[Foreign language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu
We have 374 IPO distribution and IR clients as of quarter-end, up 36% year-over-year. Of all 31 companies listed in Hong Kong in H1 2023, 20 of them have used one or more of our enterprise product offerings. In the quarter, we acted as joint bookrunners of several high-profile Hong Kong IPOs, including those of YSB and ZKH.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu
[Foreign language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu

The Japan market is characterized by its large and growing number of affluent retail investors, high penetration of online trading, and increasing penchant for US stock trading, and we are excited to tap into this immense market opportunity.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu
[Foreign language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu
Next, I'd like to invite our CFO, Arthur, to discuss our financial performance.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu
Thanks, Leaf Li and Daniel. Before going through our financial performance, I'd like to give you an update on our latest $500 million share repurchase program announced on 11 March 2022. At the end of H1, we have repurchased an aggregate of 11 million ADS with approximately $360 million total repurchase amount in open market transactions. It constitutes about 70% of the maximum purchase amount approved under our share repurchase program. Now back to the financial performance in Q2. All the numbers mentioned below are in HKD. Total revenues for the quarter were HKD 2.5 billion, up 42% from HKD 1.7 billion in Q2 2022.
Brokerage commission and handling charge income was HKD 953 million, a decrease of 80% year over year and a 12% Q over Q. The Q over Q decrease was mainly due to the decline in the total trading volume, partially offset by the increase in the blended commission rate from 8.8 basis points to 9.9 basis points. Interest income was HKD 1.4 billion, an increase of 127% year over year and 9% Q over Q. The increase was driven by higher interest income from cash deposits and higher security lending income. Other income was HKD 127 million, up 37% year over year and maintained most flat Q over Q. The year over year increase was driven by higher fund distribution income.
Other income maintained largely stable Q-over-Q, since higher fund distribution service income and the trust fee were largely offset by lower currency exchange income, underwriting fee income, and the market information and data income. Total costs were HKD 375 million, an increase of 80% from HKD 208 million in Q2 2022. Brokerage commission and handling charge expenses were HKD 55 million, down 37% year-over-year and 23% Q-over-Q. The decrease was attributable to lower trading volume and the cost saving from our US sales clearing business. Interest expenses were HKD 220 million, up 729% year-over-year, and 68% Q-over-Q. The increase was mainly driven by higher expenses associated with our securities borrowing and lending business.
Higher funding costs from margin financing business also contribute to Q-over-Q increase. Processing and servicing costs were $99 million, up 5% year-over-year and 13% Q-over-Q. The increase was primarily due to higher system usage fee, market information fee, and the data transformation fee, which also increased on a sequential basis. As a result, total gross profit was $2.1 billion, increase of 37% from $1.5 billion in Q2 2022. Gross margin was 85% as compared to 88% in Q2 2022. Operating expenses were 18% year-over-year and 6% Q-over-Q to $852 million. R&D expenses was $363 million, up 25% year-over-year and 2% Q-over-Q.
The increase was mainly due to an increase in R&D head count as we continue to upgrade our infrastructure, support new product offerings, and invest in product localization in international markets. Selling and marketing expenses was HKD 175 million, down 20% year-over-year and up 24% Q-over-Q. The year-over-year decrease was mainly due to lower customer acquisition costs, and the Q-over-Q increase was driven by accelerated client acquisition. G&A expenses was HKD 314 million, up 49% year-over-year, and 2% Q-over-Q. The increase was mainly due to increase in head count for general and administrative personnel to support our international business expansion. As a result, our total net income increased by 74% year-over-year and decreased by 6% Q-over-Q to HKD 1.1 billion.
Net income margin expanded to 45% from 37% in the same quarter last year, primarily due to strong top line growth and the lower selling and marketing expenses. That concludes our prepared remarks. We'd now like to open the call to questions. Operator, please go ahead. Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. To ask a question, please press star one one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. To withdraw your question, please press star one and one again. That's star one and one if you wish to ask a question. Please stand by while we compile a Q&A roster. We will now take the first question. One moment, please. From the line of Chiao Huang from MS, please go ahead.
Chiao Huang
Financial Advisor, MS
[Foreign language]
Let me briefly translate. The two questions regarding the trading volume, and we're seeing the trading volume slip further than the overall market in both Hong Kong and the US in Q2 for Futu. Just wondering what's the implication there. Also, I know we're seeing the brokerage commission bouncing quite sharply in Q2 and roughly what's the driving factors behind? Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu
Thank you, Chiao Huang. I will take two of your questions. Number one, regarding the trading volume, it is generally just in line with the overall market conditions. Particularly, you know, in Q2, we see the market actually is very challenging across the board, regardless in the US or in Hong Kong. What we observed is actually the trading velocity from our clients both in the US and also in Hong Kong has decreased. The situation seems to be temporary as we see the trading velocity rebound quarter to date in Q2. In terms of the trading commissions, the major reason, as we elaborate several times before, is more related to the client's trading behavior in the US stock.
As in Q2, we see more clients trading these low-value stocks in the US markets, which let the implied blended commission rate become higher versus Q2.
Chiao Huang
Financial Advisor, MS
Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. We will now take the next question from the line of You Fan from CICC. Please go ahead.
You Fan
Analyst, CICC
Okay. I will translate. Thanks, management, for taking my questions. This is You Fan from CICC. I have two questions here. The first one is regarding the AUM and revenue breakdown by assets.
[Foreign language]
How much does Hong Kong and US stocks and wealth management products and also the cash balance account for the total client assets balance? How much does Hong Kong and US stock market account for the total revenue effectively? The second question is regarding the client net assets inflow. I wonder, what's the assets inflow of clients in Hong Kong, Singapore, and also Mainland China effectively?
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu
Thank you, You Fan. I will answer your second question first, and I will leave the first question to Leaf Li. In terms of the net asset inflows in Q2, we see a very healthy rebound in Q2 versus Q1, given that we got some negative headline news in Q2, which caused certain clients uncomfortable in terms of their, you know, assets parking in our accounts. This impact has been fully removed in Q2. To break down among the different regions, Hong Kong actually contributed the most of the asset inflows, which followed by Singapore afterwards. I leave the second question to Leaf Li.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu
[Foreign language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu
In the past few quarters, the breakdown of Futu's client assets has remained relatively stable, with more client assets allocated to Hong Kong stocks than US stocks. The proportion of wealth management assets actually continued to rise in the past couple of quarters, and now accounting for about 10%, by the end of Q2, which more than doubled year-over-year. Clients' cash balance accounted for low teens of total client asset balance. To answer your question regarding the revenue breakdown between Hong Kong and US stocks, Hong Kong stocks usually contributed about 30% of the trading volume. US stocks contributed 70% of the trading volume. The blended commission rate for US stocks is slightly higher, so about 75% of our trading commission actually came from US stock trading. Thank you.
You Fan
Analyst, CICC
Okay, thank you very much.
Operator
Thank you. We will now take the next question. From the line of Cindy Wang from China Renaissance. Please go ahead.
Cindy Wang
DIrector, China Renaissance
[Foreign language] Cindy.
Thank you, management, for taking my call. This is Cindy from China Renaissance. I have two questions. First question is related to the customer acquisition cost.
